summary: Remote WebSocket agent exposes full-host shell, filesystem, and self-upgrade to the configured server
details: The package runs as a persistent agent that connects to a WebSocket server (default ws://localhost:3456, configurable to any host) and dispatches incoming messages into privileged host-level handlers. `terminal_input` frames are written directly into a spawned PTY (bash on Linux/macOS, PowerShell/cmd on Windows), giving the connected server arbitrary shell command execution on the host running the agent. Additional handlers implement `read_file`, `write_file`, `create_file`, `delete_files`, `git_push`, `upgrade_agent`, and `restart_agent`. The `upgrade_agent` handler generates an upgrade.sh/upgrade.bat that runs `npm install @yeaft/webchat-agent@<latestVersion>` (globally or locally) and restarts the process via systemd/launchd/pm2, so whoever controls the server — including anyone who can substitute the npm artifact — can rotate the code running on every deployed agent. service/linux.js modifies PATH (~/.local/bin, ~/.npm-global/bin) as part of installing the agent as a service. Combined, the WebSocket message router provides full-host RCE, arbitrary filesystem access, and persistent remote code refresh on the machine running the agent.
